searchText: Hi <@372317178906542081> , <@1361003005691822160>, EIP-8360 is PFId for Hegotá - right? yeah, would be even possibile for glamsterdam? If so we can speed up the specs Glamsterdam won't be possible, Hoodi fork is in a month 🙂 I'll try to review the current proposal, was made by <@1361003005691822160> I think adding a new opcode is more complex than simply adding a selfdestruct refund, even if simplified yeah I agree, but some core devs fear it will delay the glamsterdam release so not much can be done atm 🤷‍♂️ <@508125616940515329> <@968526635735326741> SELFDESTRUCT is PFId to be removed for good in hegota? re data I think should be fetched for every major EVM, August: 1. BNB: 115k Transactions 2. Ethereum: 36.8k Transactions 3. Arbitrum: 15k Transactions Most likely will go down on Ethereum in favor to to other networks given the very high cost increase Feedback here from Nethermind: https://gist.github.com/LukaszRozmej/9fc6b743bb82e363e16a0337bfc0bbc9 should be addressed in EIP-8360: > EIP-8360 — TCREATE Opcode · C Contracts that live for one transaction are a genuine state-hygiene win, and a cleaner path off SELFDESTRUCT than deprecation alone. But the proposal declares a dependency on EIP-7610, which was declined on 2026-08-20, and it does not yet say how a transient account appears in a block access list or under last-written-block metadata. Those need answers before it can be assessed. I think it should be swapped to EIP-684 so we fall back to that collission mechanism (EIP-7610 is the extended version of it but we rejected that version in Glamsterdam, so EIP-684 is the current spec for collisison checks) I left a comment on Magicians with some Qs regarding the current version of EIP-8360: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8360-tcreate-opcode/29258/4?u=jochem-brouwer

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content:
Feedback here from Nethermind: https://gist.github.com/LukaszRozmej/9fc6b743bb82e363e16a0337bfc0bbc9 should be addressed in EIP-8360:

> EIP-8360 — TCREATE Opcode · C Contracts that live for one transaction are a genuine state-hygiene win, and a cleaner path off SELFDESTRUCT than deprecation alone. But the proposal declares a dependency on EIP-7610, which was declined on 2026-08-20, and it does not yet say how a transient account appears in a block access list or under last-written-block metadata. Those need answers before it can be assessed.

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: I think it should be swapped to EIP-684 so we fall back to that collission mechanism (EIP-7610 is the extended version of it but we rejected that version in Glamsterdam, so EIP-684 is the current spec for collisison checks)
